items.snippet_en: GOV.UK states there is no evidence linking 5G and coronavirus, as viruses cannot travel on radio waves or mobile networks. It also notes that coronavirus is spreading in countries without 5G.
The International Telecommunication Union (ITU), a UN agency, confirmed that the theory of a link between 5G and COVID-19 is "a hoax that has no technical basis."

items.title: 5G misinformation
items.snippet_en: Wikipedia, citing the CDC, explains that 5G uses non-ionizing radiation which does not damage DNA, and there is no evidence that it affects the immune system.

AP News reported that claims of maps showing a correlation between confirmed COVID-19 cases and 5G installation are false, explaining both maps highlight densely populated areas where 5G is rolled out.

A study published in Medical Research Archives found a statistical correlation between higher COVID-19 cases and deaths in US states and counties with 5G millimeter wave wireless telecommunications, even after accounting for population density.
While one study found a statistical correlation, other sources strongly refute any causal link between 5G and increased coronavirus cases.

items.title: How false claims about 5G health risks spread into the mainstream
items.snippet_en: The Guardian reported that a claim about Wuhan being the first city to receive 5G and the origin of COVID-19 is false, as other cities had 5G earlier and countries without 5G also had high cases.

items.title: 5G technology does not cause or spread coronavirus
items.snippet_en: UNICEF Montenegro stated that their analysis shows 5G does not spread coronavirus.
